title: `nav_gate.py` certifies geometry that never ships
remainder: The gate still bakes a runtime GLTF load with PARSED_GEOMETRY_MESH_INSTANCES; the item asks that it 'should bake what the runtime loads -- instance the imported scene, or parse `PARSED_GEOMETRY_BOTH` the way the navqa scene does'.

per_piece.piece: nav_gate bakes what the runtime loads (imported scene, or PARSED_GEOMETRY_BOTH)
per_piece.evidence: deli_counter/godot/addon/deli_counter/nav_gate.gd:198-206 still loads the shell with GLTFDocument.append_from_file + generate_scene (no importer), and :223 still sets `nm.geometry_parsed_geometry_type = NavigationMesh.PARSED_GEOMETRY_MESH_INSTANCES`, with the comment at :209-211 saying the -colonly collision meshes are 'still real meshes here'. deli_counter/nav_gate.py:102-103 launches `godot --headless --script nav_gate.gd -- glb gameplay out` with no import pass. `git log -L223,226` on nav_gate.gd shows only the origin commit 51908762 (2026-07-17); the three later commits to the file (79ba672c 2026-09-14, 121f0fe5 0.189.0 grid sweep, cf109231 0.196.0 entrances) do not touch the parse. Meanwhile lot/lot.py:3266-3267 (walk scene) and :3479-3480 (navqa scene) still write `geometry_parsed_geometry_type = 2` (Lot 0.126.1, dc4e2a6), and built shells still ship collider-only nodes (deli_counter/build/07_police_station.gameplay.json:913 names `VAULTLEDGE_0-convcolonly`; DC 0.236.1's CHANGELOG at line 1068 restates that Lot bakes the walk navmesh at type 2).
per_piece.checked: Read nav_gate.gd 150-279 and nav_gate.py's Godot launch; grep for parsed_geometry_type/PARSED_GEOMETRY across lot, level_factory and deli_counter; git log of nav_gate.gd since 2026-08-14 and git log -L on the parse line; grep of the roadmap after line 1300 for GLTFDocument / PARSED_GEOMETRY / nav_gate finds no later item taking this over.

notes: Nothing has moved on this item since 2026-08-14; the newest status's lot.py:1430,1643 are now lot.py:3267,3480 (same content). Where the two bakes can actually differ: a `-colonly` node is the same triangles either way (runtime mesh vs imported trimesh collider), so the gap is a `-convcolonly` node whose source mesh is not convex (the importer's hull differs from the mesh the gate parses) plus any other import-time rewrite. Nobody has counted how many shells that changes, so the size of the defect in practice is unmeasured. The fix needs an import pass (a staged project, as Level Factory's jobs do) or equivalent, and a re-gate of the library, because the gate's results are frozen by the library's population test (nav_gate.gd:276-278: 'nav_gate.py prints it and the library's population test freezes the set') -- hence medium rather than small. Separate from item 12 (the collider mask), which shares the 'One bake, two items' section but asks for a different change.
